observation_summary: The DateUtils.truncate method incorrectly handles Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions because it relies on Calendar.set() calls, which trigger side effects (like resetting DST offsets) even when the field value remains unchanged. This causes the truncated date to shift by an hour.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces the reliance on Calendar.set() for lower-level time units (milliseconds, seconds, minutes) with direct arithmetic on the underlying time (long) value. This is a fundamental change to the computational strategy of the truncation algorithm to avoid side effects of the Calendar API. While the fix also includes a guard (if offset != 0), the primary mechanism is the rewrite of the truncation logic to avoid the problematic API calls, making it an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The bug report states that Calendar.set() resets fields like DST_OFFSET even if the value is the same.
The fix diff shows a complete rewrite of the truncation logic for milliseconds, seconds, and minutes to use direct time arithmetic instead of Calendar.set().
The fix adds a guard 'if (offset != 0)' to the existing loop, but the core fix is the new manual calculation logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a guard was added, the primary issue was the reliance on an API that caused side effects, requiring a change in the computational approach (algorithm) rather than just a missing validation.
The fix is a local procedural correction to the DateUtils.truncate method, not a design-level capability gap.
